doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: The Perseverance, Belvin Park, and how Sam Morgan replaced Jack Paeda
summary: Martin remembers minstrel shows at the Perseverance, which became Belvin Park. When trumpeter Jack Paeda fell sick for three months Sam Morgan was hired, and Paeda was not allowed to sit back in.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. Of course, first he can't remember. Of course he done forgot it. The Perseverance used to be over there on the mark in Pacific back then. Remember the Perseverance?
Yeah, I remember that. When... When y'all used to be playing back there in stumps and rags, and them used to put on them... They used to put on them minister shows, their dancers.
The band be playing back there. That's right. Well, they tore that down and put it out there Homer in Belvin, and call it the Belvin Park. That's where Jack Paidi used to play.

I don't remember, he and his father, and his brother, what is his name? Johnny Lindsay, eh? Good ass. But didn't Jack Paidi play with Johnny? No Johnny Lindsay band? Johnny Lindsay, I don't know. But I know. You know Johnny Lindsay?

In my time, I had Bill Beating Drum, Yank On Trambone. You take, uh... Oh, that boy, he died down there earlier. Julius Granderson playing banjo. I forget who was playing bass. Jack Paidi playing trumpet. Cause his team song, I'll never forget that. Cause I just was getting big enough then. I was around 20 years old then. His team song, If You Don't Like The Way I Do. Yeah. You understand? That was his team song. Cause I was like, you know, I was like, you know. You know what I was like? You know what I was like? Yeah. About seventh grade stuff 19, he gets sick and he stays sick three months. And when he come back to the band, I was at the dance that night. They done hired Sam Morgan in his place and when he come back to the band, to his band, they wouldn't let him sit in. That's where the... That's the secret house. No, no, at the Belvin Park. There where the humbug stopped. Almost had been the killing script there. Jack Paeda. That's how Sam got in that band.
They put him out of his own band.
That's how Sam got in it. I guess he didn't... They don't blame me for not liking it. That's how Sam got in it.
Yeah. Because Sam was working... He was working at the Crummer Line in the Southern Pacific then. Yeah.
Trying to make it. Yeah. A lot of work in there too. Yeah.
Bar. Jack Paeda got sick there. They taking him in there. You understand? Jack Paeda coming back. They kept saying. Yanking them. Bill was beating drums then. He wasn't on the trombone.
